 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The plant kingdom and animal kingdom are two major classifications in the biological classification system.
 
• Cellular Structure:
 
 
• Plants are generally composed of eukaryotic cells, which means their cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
 
• Animals also have eukaryotic cells, but some animal groups, such as sponges, have simpler cellular structures compared to most plants.
 
 
 
• Nutrition:
 
 
• Plants are autotrophs, meaning they can produce their own food through photosynthesis.
 
• Animals are heterotrophs and cannot produce their own food. They obtain nutrients by consuming other organisms or organic matter.
 
 
 
• Mobility:
 
 
• Plants are typically rooted in the ground and are sessile organisms.
 
• Animals, on the other hand, are generally mobile and have various locomotion strategies, ranging from walking and swimming to flying.
 
 
 
• Reproduction:
 
 
• Plants reproduce through a combination of sexual and asexual reproduction.
 
• Animals also reproduce sexually.
 
 
 
• Body Organization:
 
 
• Plants often have a modular body structure with repeated units, such as leaves, stems, and roots.
 
• Animals have a more diverse range of body plans, including specialized tissues, organs, and organ systems.
